Key Activities: Plans and conducts analysis of economic and financial statistical data and develops strategies, innovative methods and models to produce, evaluate, analyse and expand analytical outputs; evaluates analytical material for publication purposes.

Provides expert advisory and consultative services to data users, source data providers and other professionals on statistical and analytical outputs. The results of research provide input into the development of future standards,classifications and compilation methods.

Performs detailed analysis, evaluation and review of statistical methods and concepts to improve existing data and determines changes in the statistical needs of clients, assessing the impact on divisional programs and developing options and strategies to manage complex issues and multi-stakeholder relations.
Provides expert analysis and advice to senior managers in government and officials in industry, academia, other national and international institutions and special interest groups.
Line or matrix supervision of teams responsible for statistical outputs, research projects or studies and management of the financial resources attached to each project.
Represents departmental interests when presenting analytical research and modelling studies to a variety of stakeholders.

decision_making: Plans and conducts comprehensive analyses and research covering multiple areas using economic and financial data based on industrial sectors, or geographical areas.

Analyses and assesses multiple data sources using various methods and techniques to determine their fitness for use and best utilization in the production of statistical program data. Uses in depth subject-matter knowledge to distill various sets of information into a coherent set of statistically robust indicators of economic performance.

Assesses client requirements for statistical information; recommends the conduct of feasibility studies or launching of projects; defines project objectives and scope; selects and evaluates research standards and techniques to be used in the conduct of studies and in the reporting of findings as well as the analytical techniques and quantitative analytical methods to be used to integrate and interpret large volumes of data.

Determines objectives and priorities for specific studies and provides expert advice and recommendations to senior management on course of action and outcomes or on significant issues affecting statistical programs.

Develops and procures in conformity to guidelines and policies new data sources, performs updates and modifications to program content and coverage to align to international frameworks or classifications and devises new concepts, definitions, methods and models to produce, evaluate, analyze, present and extend statistical information relating to the different subject matter domains (e.g. Energy, BOP, GFS, Environment, Prices).
leadership_and_operational_management: Manages project teams responsible for statistical analysis and studies. Plans and schedules the work, resolves conflicting priorities, ascertains human resource needs, determines the appropriate selection methods (internal and external resources / contractors) to meet program and project objectives, recruits staff, monitors progress towards achieving goals and deliverables, evaluates employee performance or reviews performance evaluations prepared by subordinates and approves training plans. Participates in, and/or contributes to, international work groups in the development, revision or updating of international frameworks, concepts or classifications relating to the different subject matter domains (e.g. Energy, BOP, GFS, Environment, Prices).
communication: Liaises with internal, external and international subject-matter experts to assess issues and new developments related concepts and measurements and proposes solutions. Chairs meetings with professionals from other divisions, departments, or international organizations, to discuss current trends and developments; to acquire up-to-date knowledge of subject matter, regulations and policies relating to statistical programs; and to develop consensus on the resolution of significant issues and the setting of priorities.

Provides expert advice and recommendations to senior management on the significant issues affecting the statistical programs and submits proposals and conceives initiatives addressing the areas of concern. Explains and elaborates on statistical program findings and their practical application and interpretation for data users. This information is used as input to decision making for a vast array of economic programs and other activities such as economic and social policy development and formulation. Interprets and adapts complex statistical data and information to provide decision makers at all levels of government, business and academics with relevant and timely statistics to support decision making regarding a vast array of economic programs and initiatives and for businesses to conduct their operations.
Provides guidance to internal, external and international subject-matter experts and data users, on methods of economic and statistical analysis.
Prepares, edits and evaluates analytical material to be published by Statistics Canada.
knowledge_of_specialized_fields: In-depth knowledge of economic principles and theories, as they relate to a specialized area, to conduct comprehensive analysis of economic data for the purpose of producing reliable and relevant statistical program data and to provide expert advisory and consultative services to clients on program results and on the concepts and methods used.

Knowledge of advanced statistical theories, methods, concepts and practices which are used in the development, compilation, processing, analysis, marketing and dissemination of statistical data, in order to plan, develop and undertake research in specific areas of economic indicators.

In-depth knowledge of multiple related subject-matter areas, classification systems, concepts and international frameworks to integrate multiple data sources and ensure the overall coherence and soundness of the economic statistical program data produced.

Knowledge of quantitative analytical methods is required to integrate and interpret massive volumes of data and to provide technical advice to other professionals. Writing and editing skills to write papers, articles and reports and to determine and assess the design and content of studies, articles and reports that will be disseminated widely or published.

Knowledge of Statistics Canada's Departmental Project Management Framework (DPMF) and other methods, techniques and practices related to project management, human resources and financial management in order to plan projects/studies, manage staff, (either directly or within a matrix management environment) and administer a budget.

Knowledge of existing data bases, conceptual frameworks, and the statistical methods and procedures applicable to the work in order to plan, develop and direct a program of detailed analysis, evaluation and research, to improve existing data, develop new methods of producing, evaluating and analyzing data, develop new concepts and extend the application of divisional statistics. Knowledge is also required of other statistical programs (concepts, methods, and databases) related to the area of expertise to identify potential sources of information for special studies, to evaluate possible data conflicts, to integrate conceptually different data from other programs, to explain variances and to recommend changes to other statistical programs.
contextual_knowledge: In-depth knowledge of the multiple related subject-matter areas and of the policies and programs of key client departments in order to assist them in identifying appropriate data to meet their needs and to provide expert advice and recommendations to senior management on the significant issues affecting the sector's programs. Knowledge of data users and suppliers from various levels of government and the private sector, to provide expert advice on statistical program data results, discuss data reporting agreements and ensure understanding of their needs.

Knowledge of current and emerging socio-economic issues in Canada and internationally as they relate to a statistical program (e.g. SNA, International Trade, BOP, GFS, Prices, etc.), to understand needs for new data, analyze the potential of new data sources and assess their burden for data providers and impact on the area of specialization and share expertise with international organizations.

Knowledge of international frameworks (e.g. Energy, SNA, GFS, Environment, Prices) and their conceptual building blocks to contribute in a meaningful way to the internal and international research agenda aimed at expanding and improving concepts and compilation methods.

Knowledge of the Statistics Act and other pertinent acts such as the Corporate Returns Act and Income Tax Act, and of Statistics Canada policies to explain legislative and policy requirements to other departments, agencies, industry, members of the public and the media. Knowledge of the Statistics and Privacy Acts is particularly important with respect to the security and confidentiality of information and data provided and to ensure that they and their subordinates do not release data or information in a form that would violate the provisions of the acts.

Extensive and relevant experience managing a complex project or statistical process related to production, analysis or dissemination using statistical methods to produce outputs.
Recent and significant experience using programming languages and tools such as Python, R, SAS, SPSS or SQL for data analysis.

Responsible for outreach and collaboration with a variety of stakeholders (within the Agency, the federal, provincial-territorial or municipal governments and agencies, academia and international institutions and private organizations) in order to establish relationships to leverage new methods and data sources, understand user needs and keep abreast of economic trends and developments, and providing expert advice and analysis.

Leads complex projects involving data acquisition, integration, linkage and use of alternative data sources to respond to user needs; develops mitigation strategies to address delays and briefs senior management when cost or scope changes are necessary.
Authors analytical papers and other types of material supporting data development and dissemination.
Participates in or leads data acquisition negotiations.
Supervises directly or in a matrix environment to plan and coordinate teams responsible for statistical outputs or projects.
Directs, through subordinates, the work of a sub-division involved in statistical program operations, analysis, interpretation, marketing and dissemination.

1. Decision making: Reviews strategic directions for the management of significant surveys and recommends innovative solutions to address departmental goals and objectives. Approves survey content and design; sample estimation and imputation methods; data integration from different sources; sample sizes and allocations to maximize efficiency within resource constraints.

Provides expert recommendations and advice to senior officials and policy makers at all levels of government, business and national social agencies and academics on the socio-economic implications of surveys and studies and the effect of their results on policies, programs and regulations, on the practical application and interpretation of statistical data and information, on advanced analytical methods and techniques and the relevancy of their use in order to develop research or analytical projects.

Directs the conduct of in-depth and unique surveys in an area of specialization or wide-ranging and extensive reviews extending across a number of subject matter areas and determines the broad objectives and content of projects and develops solutions to complex methodology issues.
Defends proposals for the development of new surveys and negotiates the allocation of funding for the conduct of projects.

Directs the review and assessment of the overall quality and completeness of statistical program results. Develops recommendations for senior management on the objectives, content, and approaches of survey programs in order to develop new statistical information or programs or expand existing programs, and data concepts and definitions to be included in the programs.
2. Leadership and operational management: Directs, through subordinates, the work of a sub-division involved in high profile surveys and projects. Reviews strategic directions for the management of significant surveys and determines the parameters, priorities, broad objectives and extent of such surveys.

Develops long term plans and objectives and allocates human resources requirements to ensure that these goals are met. Directs recruitment activities for both, permanent and project team staff, and approves training and development plans. Prepares performance appraisals for subordinate staff, reviews performance appraisals prepared by subordinate supervisors, and resolves performance and disciplinary matters.

Plans, develops and manages budgets for projects, including estimates for salaries, professional fees and implementation costs, with authority to allocate/reallocate funds as needed. Submits cost estimates and projections to senior management and authorises expenditures in accordance with approved budgets.

Negotiates and approves contracts with consulting firms and for the acquisition of services. Selects contractors for specific projects, assigns, directs, manages and evaluates the work according to contract specifications.
3. Communication: Mediates with senior executives of major Canadian corporations, representatives of private sector associations, federal, provincial and municipal government departments, unions and universities to establish joint survey agreements, to maintain good relations and cooperation with the user community and data suppliers, to promote an understanding of programs, to market statistical products and services, and to monitor relevant concepts and practices related to the use and application of program results.

As a departmental representative, explains the results and statistical methods and approaches used in the conduct of studies and surveys to all levels of government, international organizations, the media and public. At this level, there is a particular requirement to deal with sensitive and political issues that could embarrass the department.

Defends proposals for the development of new surveys to address current socio-economic trends and developments at the national and international levels, and negotiates the allocation of funding for the conduct of such surveys and projects. Presents arguments and options and negotiates resources and timeframes for large-scale projects requiring the participation of data suppliers. It is not unusual to encounter resistance on the part of data suppliers. Major difficulties can be encountered as the projects involve the negotiation of significant resources and services with multiple milestones.

Writes analytical papers and articles on the interpretation of statistical surveys or projects and their application to the area of specialization and presents analytical material to media representatives to maintain the department’s reputation where there is a particular requirement to deal with sensitive and political issues that could embarrass the department.
Chairs intra-departmental meetings and participates in inter-departmental meetings, conferences and groups to develop consensus or share knowledge in a particular field.
4. Knowledge of specialized fields: Expert knowledge of advanced economic or sociology theories and principles relating to a specialized subject area to provide authoritative and expert advice to senior officials and policy advisors within and outside Statistics Canada on the results of unique economic and socio-economic studies and their impact on major program, policy or regulatory issues and to define the objectives, content and approaches of unique and complex analytical projects covering a broad area of specialization or a range of departmental statistical programs, to improve existing concepts or develop new concepts, to extend the application of statistics and to analyze data.

A deep understanding of the underlying theoretical concepts of economics, sociology and statistics as they relate to a group of specialized areas to develop and implement programs to produce statistics covering a wide range of issues.

A comprehensive knowledge of economic and social information to develop and implement programs to produce statistics depicting Canada’s population, labour force, economic life, education, housing, transportation and social and cultural life.

Knowledge of writing and editing skills and techniques to write and review papers, articles and reports and to determine and assess the design and content of studies, articles and reports that will be disseminated widely or published.

Knowledge of the principles and practices of management with regards to human and financial resources in order to direct the work of a sub-division through subordinate section chiefs, and/or multi-disciplinary departmental and interdepartmental project teams, working groups and committees.
5. Contextual knowledge: Knowledge of current and emerging socio-economic and political issues in Canada in relation to that of other industrialized countries such as the changed social context and the globalization of markets, particularly as they relate to all the aspects of a variety of statistical programs. This knowledge is necessary to defend proposals for the development of new surveys.

Knowledge of governmental policies, programs and regulatory issues in order to provide expert advice to senior officials and policy advisors, within and outside Statistics Canada, on the results and impact of unique economic and socio-economic studies.
Knowledge of the division mandate and priorities as well as subject-matter expertise is required to review strategic directions in the management of significant surveys.

Knowledge of the policies and programs of key client departments in order to mediate with their representatives to reach a consensus on the major issues affecting departments, industries and special interest groups, and to recommend priorities for new surveys and studies.

Knowledge of the Statistics Act is needed to explain the legislative requirements to other departments, agencies, industry, members of the public and the media. This knowledge, along with knowledge of the Privacy Act is also required to ensure that the organization meets its commitment to ensuring the confidentiality of all information provided to them and does not release any information that identifies an individual or group without prior consent.
Knowledge of a variety of Acts related to the area of expertise such as the Income Tax Act, the Excise Sales Tax Act, the Employment Insurance Act, and the Corporate Returns Act.
6. Research and analysis: Analyses current socio-economic trends and developments at the national and international levels and determines the implications of proposed areas of study. Analyses user needs in relation to current socio-economic trends and developments at the national and international levels, translates them into a concrete, timely and affordable information request, determines the implications of proposed areas of study and defends proposals for the development of new surveys.
Provides expert analysis and interpretation of program results, develops the overall conclusions and recommendations, reviews and approves analytical material and research papers for publication.
Directs the development of new methods and techniques for unique studies, assesses the implications of new approaches and develops solutions to complex issues.

Analyses the impact of study results on major program, policy and regulatory issues and provides authoritative and expert advice to senior officials and policy advisors within and outside Statistics Canada.

7. PHYSICAL Effort: Frequent, extended periods of sitting at a work station while keyboarding, proofreading, telephoning, reviewing data, or writing text.
Occasional periods of physical exertion, such as bending and stretching to retrieve, organize and distribute publications, printouts, documents or files.
There may be an occasional requirement to carry equipment, presentation material and document cases to meetings or during travel.
8. SENSORY Effort: There is an occasional requirement for sensory observation when comparing old and new versions of data.
9. WORKING CONDITIONS: The work is performed in an open office environment with constant exposure to glare from a computer screen, noise from conversations, telephones, traffic and equipment in the immediate area.
Work is performed while facing multiple and sometimes competing demands from clients, frequent changes in methods, systems and approaches and competing priorities and changing deadlines.
There is a requirement to travel nationally and/or internationally, several times a year for several days at a time.

Encounters resistance from external clients or respondents who may be impatient, irritated or uncooperative, as well as program criticism from clients, the media, and members of the public and special interest groups.

Negotiates cost reductions and arranges contracts with consulting firms and for the acquisition of services. Selects contractors for specific projects, assigns, directs, manages and evaluates the work according to contract specifications.
3. Communication: Provides expert advisory and consultative services to policy makers at all levels of government, business and national social agencies and academia. Explains and elaborates on statistical program findings and their practical application and interpretation of statistical data and information. This information is used as input to decision making for a vast array of economic and social policies, programs and other activities.

Writes and presents subject matter and technical concepts, definitions and terms in common terminology in order to explain and clarify developmental projects and operational systems and processes or program results. When findings are challenged or misinterpreted, it is necessary to present logical arguments to justify the results and to defend the validity of statistical methods and approaches used in order to maintain the department’s reputation for producing high quality data.
Chairs intra-departmental meetings and participates in inter-departmental meetings, conferences and groups to develop understanding, consensus and share knowledge of the program area.
4. Knowledge of specialized fields: Knowledge of economic or sociology principles and theory to provide expert advisory and consultative services to clients on program results and on the concepts and methods used in mass data processing.

Extensive knowledge of current and emerging socio-economic issues in Canada and internationally, such as the changing social context and the globalization of markets, particularly as they relate to all the aspects of a statistical program. This knowledge is required to analyze program outputs, anticipate and understand needs for new data, and assess the impact on the area of specialization.

Advanced knowledge of systems analysis and design and of new and emerging computer technology and applications in order to establish and manage mass statistical data collection, production and dissemination environments.
Knowledge of the principles and practices of project management including the management of human and financial resources.
5. Contextual knowledge: Knowledge of the departmental and divisional mandate, activities, priorities, practices, standards and procedures applicable to the work to incorporate them into the management of a statistical program and to recommend changes to management.

Knowledge of other statistical programs (concepts, methods, and databases) related to the area of expertise to plan and implement statistical activities, to integrate conceptually different data from other programs, to explain variances and to recommend changes to other statistical programs.

Knowledge of Statistics Canada policies, (e.g. confidentiality of data, security, respondent relations, and data quality), practices and classification systems is required to ensure that they are applied in the conduct of production and dissemination activities.
Knowledge of the policies and programs of key client departments is needed to determine their information requirements.

Knowledge of data users from governments and from the private sector to identify potential new markets, to understand client needs for statistical data or studies, to negotiate contracts and to provide expert advice on program results.

Knowledge of the Statistics Act is needed to explain the legislative requirements to data suppliers/users, and to negotiate special agreements. This knowledge, along with knowledge of the Privacy Act is also required to ensure that the organization meets its commitment to ensuring the confidentiality of all information provided to them and does not release any information that identifies an individual or group without prior consent.
Knowledge of a variety of Acts related to the area of expertise such as the Income Tax Act, the Excise Sales Tax Act, the Employment Insurance Act, and the Corporate Returns Act.
6. Research and analysis: Reviews the conceptual framework of existing statistical programs and determines the need for development, modification and adaption. Programs involve a combination of statistical techniques and methods and the integration of data from a variety of sources (e.g. financial statements, tax files, other administrative sources, surveys, censuses). Source data have often been collected for other purposes using different definitions or concepts and must be translated into common concepts, taking into consideration the impact of the result on other statistical programs as well as departmental priorities.

Assesses new statistical methods, techniques and practices and the associated costs and limitations and identifies the availability and reliability of new data sources to evaluate the suitability of new hardware and software and to determine the short and long term program impact and benefits.

Analyses the relative quality of data produced by statistical programs, determines reasons for variances; reviews the comparability of data over time and relevance in light of trends, developments, changing requirements, policy issues and socio-economic conditions.

Researches gaps and inconsistencies in the production and dissemination methods and procedures, reviews the conceptual framework used and the compatibility with other statistical programs. Problems to be resolved usually impact on other statistical programs.
Investigates client requirements for statistical information and determines the capacity and ability of existing or modified systems to meet these requirements.

Education: Successful completion of two years of a post secondary program with acceptable specialization in social science, statistics, library/archival work or a law related field.
An acceptable combination of education, training and/or experience.
Experience: Extensive and relevant experience managing a complex process or service related to the processing and dissemination of business data.
Extensive experience managing multiple cost recovery business data related projects simultaneously.

Extensive experience managing or leading a multidisciplinary team to process business data and produce custom tabulations for multiple ad hoc business surveys simultaneously in a cost recovery environment.
Extensive experience providing subject matter expertise related to business data production and data editing, as well as survey operational processes, such as planning, development, and coordination.
Extensive experience providing consultative services to internal or external users regarding the processing and tabulations of business data in a cost recovery environment.
